2026-10-03T17:29:31.3883123Z       "body": "Fixes #12642.\r\n\r\nRewrites `SyncBranchesToDB` with two major changes:\r\n- Rather than using the in-memory commit from the `post-receive` hook, it queries the authoritative git repository for the current state of the branch.\r\n- Locks on the repo\u0026branch to prevent concurrent updates, preventing reading a state from the git repo, it becoming stale, and then writing it to the DB.  (More technically, this series of operations can still happen, but a second update to the branch will be blocked behind this and will correct the state.)\r\n\r\nThere is a performance risk with this approach.  With the previous implementation, if a push to a branch had the same commit ID provided to the post-receive hook as the database already stored, there would be no git operation.  With the new operation, `SyncBranchesToDB` will always check the git repo branch state (re-using a `git cat-file-batch` process to perform this check for multiple branches).\r\n\r\n`TestGitPushConcurrentBranchUpdate` triggers this behaviour through a somewhat synthetic test; a \"[test seam](https://www.informit.com/articles/article.aspx?p=359417\u0026seqNum=2)\" is provided to allow the test to freeze the first push from a git repo.  The term \"test seam\" is used here because my go-to of a \"hook\" is confusing in the Forgejo context where `post-receive` *is* git hook, plus we have custom git hooks, and webhooks, all using the term \"hook\". 🤣\r\n\r\n### Compliance\r\n\r\n- [x] I confirm that I make this contribution in accordance with [Forgejo's AI Agreement](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/governance/src/commit/9084720dc6a7fbf1d3f358919d46bd6adfb55287/AIAgreement.md).\r\n\r\n### Tests for Go changes\r\n\r\n- I added test coverage for Go changes...\r\n  - [ ] in their respective `*_test.go` for unit tests.\r\n  - [x] in the `tests/integration` directory if it involves interactions with a live Forgejo server.\r\n- I ran...\r\n  - [x] `make pr-go` before pushing\r\n\r\n### Documentation\r\n\r\n- [ ] I created a pull request [to the documentation](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/docs) to explain to Forgejo users how to use this change.\r\n- [x] I did not document these changes and I do not expect someone else to do it.\r\n\r\n### Release notes\r\n\r\n- [x] This change will be noticed by a Forgejo user or admin (feature, bug fix, performance, etc.). I suggest to include a release note for this change.\r\n- [ ] This change is not visible to a Forgejo user or admin (refactor, dependency upgrade, etc.). I think there is no need to add a release note for this change.\r\n\r\n",
